extracted.intended_audience: attorneys who practice before the USPTO; Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) staff; disciplinary enforcement bodies
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 — when the USPTO may impose discipline identical to a state court's lawyer-discipline order, the standards for doing so, required notices, and the scope/effect of the suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a duly constituted authority of a State (here, the Supreme Court of Nevada's order), pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 and 35 U.S.C. § 32.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the facts and discipline imposed by the state court are established and there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), the USPTO Director may impose identical discipline for practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond and 40-day response period
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice and Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 must be sent to the respondent and provide an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent in this matter received the Notice and Order and filed a timely letter dated July 15, 2019. Responses may invoke the grounds in § 11.24(d)(1) to oppose reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds to oppose reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may oppose imposition of identical discipline based on one or more reasons enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This document references § 11.24(d)(1) as the statutory list of defenses (not reproduced here); the respondent must invoke those defenses within the prescribed period to create a genuine issue of material fact preventing automatic reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine issue of material fact standard (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), it is appropriate for the USPTO to impose reciprocal discipline identical to the state order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's statement that he is 'amenable to the imposition of discipline identical' and that 'there is no genuine issue of material fact' supported the determination to impose identical discipline in this case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and duration of USPTO suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from the practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO for one year, stayed for eighteen months subject to conditions, effective the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The stayed suspension is conditioned on successful compliance with the conditions set by the Supreme Court of the State of Nevada during the eighteen-month stay. The Order expressly notes Mr. Randazza 'is not authorized to practice before the Office in patent matters.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicate violation cited: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: The discipline is for violating 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon being suspended (stayed) from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice summarizes the factual basis: knowingly violating duties to his client (conflict of interest) and the legal profession (restrictions on the right to practice) arising from loaning money to a client without informing the client in writing of the desirability of obtaining independent counsel, and negotiating to receive a retainer for future legal services as part of a settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette publication requirement and content consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is 'materially consistent' with the sample 'Notice of Stayed Suspension' provided in the Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample notice must include respondent's name and residence, authorization to practice in trademark/non-patent matters, the suspension order (duration and stay), the regulatory citation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)), a concise statement of the basis for discipline (including the factual misconduct), a statement about patent practice authorization, and a link to where disciplinary decisions are publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where respondent is admitted, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a required administrative step to ensure relevant jurisdictions and the public are informed of the USPTO's disciplinary action and its reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of disciplinary decisions (OED FOIA Reading Room)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room (https://foiadocuments.uspto.gov/oed/).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice should reference where the public can access full disciplinary decisions; the Order directs publication of that link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of respondent's consent on imposition
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent's explicit amenability to identical discipline and failure to identify genuine factual disputes supports the USPTO's imposition of reciprocal discipline without further contested proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter, respondent's concession that identical discipline was appropriate led the Director to conclude there was no genuine issue of material fact and to impose the same disciplinary terms as the state court.
